newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down led by blue chips.

text.p: Czech blue chip issues pulled the PX50 and RPIX indices lower on Wednesday with dealers attributing the declines to lower demand from abroad.
The four most heavily capitalised shares on the PX50 followed Tuesday's falls with further losses after posting strong gains in the first six trading sessions of the year.
"There has been a correction in all blue chips," said Karel Ruzicka from ING Barings.
"(There has been) quite good supply for CEZ for example coming from local dealers and demand from abroad has been lower in the last few days," he added.
CEZ fell 14 crowns, 1.3 percent, to 1,049, Komercni Banka lost 46 crowns, 1.9 percent, to 2,331, SPT Telecom dropped 10 crowns to 3,360 and Ceska Sporitelna lost one crown to 329.

In the broader market, brewery Radegast continued to slip back after some strong gains on a Bass anouncement last week that it wished to increase its stake in the Czech brewer from the 33 percent which it recently acquired.

Bass said on Wednesday that it was not trying to raise its stake in Radegast through the capital markets where liquidity is extremely low and would concentrate on negotiations with the biggest shareholder, IPB, to achieve its objectives.
Overall, turnover was relatively high at 1.2 billion crowns.
